title: Canto 1: Creation - Title, Artist and Source Pictures Canto 1
content:
Title, Artist and Source Pictures Canto 1​

Acknowledgements

Title: Lord Kṛṣṇa lifting Govardhana Hill

Artist: Unknown

Source: Facebook Vrindavan das

Introduction:

Title: Lord Kṛṣṇa

Artist: Probably an art work by Raja Ravi Varma

Source: Wikipedia Raja Ravi Varma

=================================

1.1

Title: 'Sages listen to Sūta Gosvāmī in the forest of Naimiṣāraṇya'

Artist: Hare Kṛṣṇa Gallery

Source: harekrsna.com

1.2

Title: Detail of a painting called: 'Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and Indra Pray to Adi Devī'

Type: Tantric Devi Series.

Artist: Kailash Raj

Source: exoticindiaart.com, used with permission.

1.3

Title: 'Yantra of Lord Viṣṇu with Twenty-four Avatāras'

Type: Collage of two vintage images and a picture

Artist: Anand Aadhar Prabhu

Source: exoticindiaart.com, used with permission.

1.4

Title: Ṛṣi Nārada

Artist: B.K. Mitra

Source: Unknown

1.5

Title: ‘Vyāsa conversing with Nārada’

Type: Sacred Art of India

Artist: Dominique Amendola, used with permission

Source: dominiqueamendola.com

1.6

Title: Elephant herd

Artist: Kailash Raj

Source: exoticindiaart.com

1.7

Title: The painting of Arjuna arresting Aśvatthāmā, and the painting of him being banned

Type: Original illustrations to the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, Basoli, c. 1750.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet

1.8

Title: ‘House of Lac’, showing Kuntī and the Pāṇḍavas leaving the house of lac set afire by the Kauravas

Artist: Nanda Lāl Bose

Source: 'Myths of the Hindus and Buddhists', Ballantine Press, Oct. 1913.

1.9

Title: Kṛṣṇa standing near Bhīṣma on the arrow bed

Artist: B.K. Mitra

Source: Unknown

1.10

Title: (detail of painting titled) “Oh, Govind! Oh, Damodar! Oh, Madhav!”

Artist: Unknown

Source: exoticindiaart.com, used with permission.

1.11

Title: 'The sacred town and temples of Dvārakā".

Artist: William Purser (1809-1837)

Source: British Library Online Gallery. Britishmuseum.org

1.12

Title: "Scenes from the Life of Kṛṣṇa: Celebrations in Honor of Kṛṣṇa's Birth", Central India, 1680-90.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Virginia Museum of Fine Arts

1.13

Title: The picture shows Gāndhārī who blindfolded herself in following her blind husband.

Artist: Nanda Lāl Bose - wikipedia.org

Source: Kamat’s Potpourri. Kamat.com

1.14

Title: ‘Yudhiṣṭhira’.

Artist: Nanda Lāl Bose - wikipedia.org

Source: 'Myths of the Hindus and Buddhists', Ballantine Press, Oct. 1913

1.15

Title: The first image is of ‘A sad Arjuna’ and the second is a painting of ‘Kṛṣṇa with the Pāṇḍavas as the legs of His horse’.

Artist: Vlad Holst, used with permission.

Source: Ten Dreams.org

1.16

Title: Photo montage/collage of a (holy) bull, a cow and a statue of Bhudevi, against the background of a landscape painted by Vrindavan das

Artists: Anand Aadhar Prabhu & Vrindavan das (used with permission)

Source: wikimedia.org & vrindavanart.com

1.17

Title: The painting indicating Parīkṣit controlling Kali. It is titled: “The Rout of the Rebel Angels”. ​
Type: Illustrations to Milton's "Paradise Lost", The Thomas Set, object 7.

Artist: William Blake

Source: William Blake Archive. blakearchive.org

1.18

Title: “A Prince and his Retinue Hunting Waterfowl”.

Type: Mughal (Murshibad), 1750-75

Artist: Unknown

Source: Virginia Museum of Fine Arts

1.19

Title: Śukadeva Reciting the Bhāgavata Purāṇa.

Type: (Ancient Stories of the Lord) to Savant Singh" (Reigned 1748-1757), 1750-1775 India, Rajasthan, Kishangarh, South Asia.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
